Detailed entries for `QPKG-021..QPKG-027`. Each follows the four-part
**What / Why / How / When NOT to apply** shape. Hooks live in
`package_routines`; the installer is `shared/scripts/qinstall.sh` in
[qnap-dev/QDK](https://github.com/qnap-dev/QDK). "QDK guide" means its
`docs/QDK-Developer-Guide.md`.

---

## QPKG-021 — Keep mutable data out of shipped files

**What.** Runtime data (databases, caches, user uploads) lives in
directories created by a hook (`pkg_install` or `start`), never in files or
directories shipped in the package. Data that must survive an uninstall
lives outside `.qpkg/<name>`, normally on a share the user chooses.

**Why.** An upgrade installs over the old version and removes shipped files
that are now obsolete; directories created by hooks are not tracked, so
upgrades leave them alone (QDK guide Cookbook, "Include a directory for
run-time data"). Uninstall deletes the whole package directory with
`rsync --delete` (QPKG-026), so data kept there is lost when the user
uninstalls, even to reinstall.

**How.**

```sh
pkg_install() {
    mkdir -p "$SYS_QPKG_DIR/data"
}
# service script: data the user owns goes on a share
DATA=$(/sbin/getcfg SHARE_DEF defVolMP -f /etc/config/def_share.info)/AppData/$QPKG_NAME
```

**When NOT to apply.** Caches that are cheap to rebuild can live inside the
package directory.

---

## QPKG-022 — List every shipped config file in `QPKG_CONFIG`

**What.** Each config file the package ships and the user may edit is listed
in `qpkg.cfg` as `QPKG_CONFIG` (repeatable). A config generated at install
time is listed too, and the package is built with `--force-config`. When you
add `QPKG_CONFIG` to a package that already has users, adopt their existing
file in `pkg_init` with `add_qpkg_config FILE <original-md5>`.

**Why.** Without it, an upgrade overwrites the user's edits with the
shipped default. With it, QDK keeps an edited file and saves the new default
beside it as `.qdksave`; a file that was untracked before becomes `.qdkorig`
(QDK guide §7). QuObjects works around the missing lifecycle by hand: its
`pkg_post_install` renames a default only when the real file is absent, and
a comment admits that an upgrade still overwrites its `proxy-server.conf`.

**How.**

```sh
# qpkg.cfg
QPKG_CONFIG="etc/myapp.conf"
```

```sh
qbuild --strict --force-config   # when etc/myapp.conf is created at install time
```

**When NOT to apply.** Files the user never edits (shipped defaults the app
reads only as a fallback) need no tracking.

---

## QPKG-023 — Detect an upgrade from the old `Version` in `qpkg.conf`

**What.** `pkg_pre_install` decides between a fresh install and an upgrade by
reading the package's existing `Version` from `qpkg.conf` with `getcfg`: empty
means a fresh install. It does not test whether `$SYS_QPKG_DIR` exists.

**Why.** `pre_install` in `qinstall.sh` (QDK 2.5.3) runs
`mkdir -p $SYS_QPKG_DIR` before it calls `pkg_pre_install`, so inside the
hook the directory always exists and a `[ -d "$SYS_QPKG_DIR" ]` test treats
every fresh install as an upgrade. QDK makes its own check before that
`mkdir`. The service is already stopped when `pkg_pre_install` runs, so it is
the safe place to back up or migrate data before new files land.

**How.**

```sh
pkg_pre_install() {
    OLD_VER=$($CMD_GETCFG "$QPKG_NAME" Version -d "" -f "$SYS_QPKG_CONFIG_FILE")
    if [ -n "$OLD_VER" ] && [ -d "$SYS_QPKG_DIR/data" ]; then
        cp -a "$SYS_QPKG_DIR/data" "$SYS_QPKG_DIR/data.pre-$OLD_VER"
    fi
}
```

**When NOT to apply.** A package with no data and no migration has nothing to
branch on.

## QPKG-024 — Abort an install with `err_log`

**What.** A hook that must stop the install or upgrade calls
`err_log "message"`. It never calls `exit` and never relies on a non-zero
return.

**Why.** Hook return values are discarded (QDK guide §6). `err_log` writes
the message to the system log, shows it in the web UI, restores the backed-up
config and aborts. An `exit` inside a hook can leave a half-installed package
with no message to the user.

**How.**

```sh
pkg_check_requirement() {
    [ "$(getconf PAGESIZE)" -le 65536 ] || err_log "unsupported kernel page size"
}
```

**When NOT to apply.** Never for aborting. A hook that only wants to warn
logs with `log_tool` (QPKG-031) and returns.

## QPKG-025 — Escape runtime values in `PKG_*_REMOVE` blocks

**What.** Inside `PKG_PRE_REMOVE`, `PKG_MAIN_REMOVE` and `PKG_POST_REMOVE`,
every variable or command meant to run at uninstall time is escaped as
`\$VAR` or `\$(cmd)`.

**Why.** These blocks are expanded when the package is built and written into
`.uninstall.sh` (QDK guide §6). An unescaped `$QPKG_ROOT` or `$(getcfg ...)`
is frozen to the build host's value, so the uninstall runs against the wrong
path or deletes nothing.

**How.**

```sh
PKG_POST_REMOVE="{
    rm -f \$(/sbin/getcfg SHARE_DEF defVolMP -f /etc/config/def_share.info)/.myapp-cache
}"
```

**When NOT to apply.** Values that really are fixed at build time (the
package name) may stay unescaped.

---

## QPKG-026 — Uninstall removes exactly what the package added

**What.** The `remove` branch (QPKG-013) and `PKG_*_REMOVE` blocks undo every
change the package made outside its directory: cron lines (QPKG-032),
`/etc/config` entries, web-server includes, symlinks. They leave user data
on shares alone, and the package documents whether data survives an
uninstall.

**Why.** `.uninstall.sh` itself removes only the package directory, its
`/etc/init.d` link, the `QS*`/`QK*` rc links and its icons (`qinstall.sh`).
Anything else stays on the NAS and can break the next install or another
package. QuObjects appends an `Include` to the system Apache config and has
to strip it again on remove. Deleting a share the user put data on is
unrecoverable.

**How.**

```sh
PKG_POST_REMOVE="{
    sed -i '/myapp-job/d' /etc/config/crontab && crontab /etc/config/crontab
    rm -f /etc/config/myapp.conf   # shipped from the build tree's config/ dir
}"
```

**When NOT to apply.** Never. Even a package that touches nothing outside
its directory should state that in its docs.

## QPKG-027 — Know that a fresh install is enabled and started

**What.** Expect a fresh install to be enabled and started immediately. A
package that needs setup before its first start (credentials, a chosen data
path) sets `SYS_QPKG_SERVICE_ENABLED="FALSE"` in a hook for fresh installs,
and asks the user to enable it after setup.

**Why.** The QDK guide (§7) says a fresh install is disabled by default, but
the code does the opposite: `get_qpkg_status` reads `Enable` with a default of
`TRUE`, and `set_qpkg_status` then enables and starts the package
(`qinstall.sh`, QDK 2.5.3). A package written to the guide starts with no
configuration on first install.

**How.**

```sh
pkg_pre_install() {
    # get_qpkg_status already ran; set_qpkg_status reads this after the hooks
    [ -n "$($CMD_GETCFG "$QPKG_NAME" Version -d "" -f "$SYS_QPKG_CONFIG_FILE")" ] ||
        SYS_QPKG_SERVICE_ENABLED="FALSE"
}
```

**When NOT to apply.** A package that starts safely with defaults, as most
should, can keep the default.
